title: Transcriptomic landscape around wound bed defines regenerative versus non-regenerative outcomes in mouse digit amputation.
authors: Prabahar, Archana; Chamberlain, Connie S; Vanderby, Ray; Murphy, William L; Dangelo, William; Mangesh, Kulkarni; Brown, Bryan; Mazumder, Barsanjit; Badylak, Stephen; Jiang, Peng
one_liner_zh: 该文通过RNA-seq和深度学习模型研究小鼠截肢后再生差异，虽涉及转录因子富集，但核心是组织再生转录组而非蛋白质-DNA互作建模，方法仅为转录组预测，与本课题关联较弱。
abstract: In the mouse distal terminal phalanx (P3), it remains mystery why amputation at less than 33% of the digit results in regeneration, while amputation exceeding 67% leads to non-regeneration. Unraveling the molecular mechanisms underlying this disparity could provide crucial insights for regenerative medicine. In this study, we aim to investigate the tissues within the wound bed to understand the tissue microenvironment associated with regenerative versus non-regenerative outcomes. We employed a P3-specific amputation model in mice, integrated with time-series RNA-seq and a macrophage assay challenged with pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokines, to explore these mechanisms. Our findings revealed that non-regenerative digits exhibit a greater intense early transcriptional response in the wound bed compared to regenerative ones. Furthermore, early macrophage phenotypes differ distinctly between regenerative and non-regenerative outcomes. Regenerative digits also display unique co-expression modules related to Bone Morphogenetic Protein 2 (Bmp2). The differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between regenerative and non-regenerative digits are enriched in targets of several transcription factors, such as HOXA11 and HOXD11 from the HOX gene family, showing a time-dependent pattern of enrichment. These transcription factors, known for their roles in bone regeneration, skeletal patterning, osteoblast activity, fracture healing, angiogenesis, and key signaling pathways, may act as master regulators of the regenerative gene signatures. Additionally, we developed a deep learning AI model capable of predicting post-amputation time and level from RNA-seq data, indicating that the regenerative probability may be "encoded" in the transcriptomic response to amputation.
abstract_zh: 在小鼠远端末节指骨（P3）中，截肢少于指骨33%时导致再生，而超过67%时导致非再生，这一现象背后的机制仍属未解之谜。揭示这种差异背后的分子机制可为再生医学提供关键见解。在本研究中，我们旨在探究伤口床内的组织，以理解与再生和非再生结果相关的组织微环境。我们采用小鼠P3特异性截肢模型，结合时间序列RNA-seq和用促炎及抗炎细胞因子挑战的巨噬细胞实验，来探索这些机制。我们的发现表明，与再生指骨相比，非再生指骨在伤口床中表现出更强烈的早期转录反应。此外，再生和非再生结果之间的早期巨噬细胞表型存在显著差异。再生指骨还显示出与骨形态发生蛋白2（Bmp2）相关的独特共表达模块。再生和非再生指骨之间的差异表达基因（DEGs）富集于多个转录因子的靶标中，例如HOX基因家族中的HOXA11和HOXD11，并显示出时间依赖性的富集模式。这些转录因子已知在骨再生、骨骼模式形成、成骨细胞活性、骨折愈合、血管生成和关键信号通路中发挥作用，可能作为再生基因特征的master regulators。此外，我们开发了一个深度学习AI模型，能够从RNA-seq数据预测截肢后时间和水平，表明再生概率可能“编码”在截肢的转录组反应中。
